frames.narration: A fan joined the waiting room before the sale opened and got a random place in line. When the sale opens, the room admits people at a fixed rate. This fan's turn comes and they receive a signed token that is valid for 15 minutes.
The fan sees the seat map. It comes from a cache that is one or two seconds old, so the fan is served instantly and the database is not touched.
The fan clicks seat A12. The booking service checks the token and tries to claim the seat with one conditional update: set the holder and a 10-minute expiry, but only if the seat is free.
The claim succeeds. A split second earlier another fan clicked A12 as well, and that claim failed because this one had already changed the row. The fan now has a hold and a ten-minute countdown.
The fan pays. The booking service creates a payment tagged with the order id and sends it to the payment service. If the fan presses Pay twice, the second is recognised by the same id.
The payment succeeds. The booking service turns the hold into a sale, but only if this fan still holds the seat and the hold has not expired.
A ticket is created with a signed code that the entry scanner can check without the internet. The fan receives it, and the seat map cache will show A12 as taken within a second or two.
Another fan holds seat B3 but wanders off. Ten minutes later a background job finds the expired hold and puts B3 back on sale, so a fan still waiting can get it.
